text:
Maya: Heads-up from a convo with Keystone (payments). They want to buy per-endpoint guarantees: a hard throughput cap + an optional low-latency add-on per route.
Zach: Got it. Two pieces then 
(1) enforcement for caps, (2) reserved capacity for low-latency lanes.
Iris: Billing note: invoices today are account-level only. We need usage export tagged by endpoint_id to show line items.
Connor: Runtime can tag requests, but billing pipeline needs a join key. Small mapper should do it.
Maya: Proposed launch scope (MVP): API flag to mark a route as capped/priority, billing export includes endpoint line items for pilot, contract template with SLA & credit formula, ops runbook for fallback.
Zach: Timeline: realistic for a pilot in 6 weeks if we keep UI minimal (no self-serve purchase). +3w for purchase flow.
Iris: Credit calc suggestion: credit = min(1.5 * endpoint_monthly_fee, charges_for_route). LegalBot: noted. We prefer clear cap on credits and enumerated endpoints in order form.
Connor: Tech checklist:
```
- add endpoint_id to usage export
- accept route_sla_role param (none|capped|priority)
- enforce cap in quota service
- label metrics with endpoint_id
```
Maya: Launch criteria quick: 3 pilot customers, endpoint line items on invoices, runbook + SRE sign-off, contract template approved.
Zach: Resource ask: backend 3w, billing eng 1w, small frontend 2w, PM + legal 
Iris: Risk: accounting mapping for many endpoints and ops load if customers buy lots of routes. Keep pilot limited to 3 endpoints per customer.
Maya: I'll pitch the pilot constraint to Keystone. Connor, can you spike the mapper this week?
Connor: Yes, will PR a spike by Fri.
Iris: I'll draft the contract clause and send to Legal for a quick review.
LegalBot: Contract draft requested. Include credit multiplier and explicit enumeration of endpoints.
Maya: Thanks all. Locking scope to MVP for pilot; will follow up after Keystone sync.
